messages.subject: Shiny - gvisScatterChart dynamic vAxis title
parts:
I had unexpected difficulty displaying different vAxis labels based on selectInput selections on a gvisScatterChart in a Shiny app.

The problem apparently was providing the vAxis "title" attribute of the gvisScatterChart() options list with a properly formatted JSON string.

With the help of an SO answer -- noted in the code snippet below -- I finally managed to do this by building a JSON string with the RJSONIO package's toJSON() method. This is indicated in bold in the relevant code snippet below from the server.R script.

Although this works, I had to (re-)cast a variable that already was a character with as.character(), so I'm wondering if I've made a (simple?) mistake that might catch up with me later.

I'll appreciate any insight on a better/standard way to do this.


# ---- from server.R ----

:
:
library(RJSONIO)
:
:
output$googleView <- renderGvis({

# filter the original dataset for the current raceway selection
  filtered.data <- myData %>% filter(tank %in% cbData())

# get the index of the current WQ property selection from nameToCode
# FYI, nameToCode is a list that collects display-able strings of water quality parameters
  idx<-which(nameToCode == input$mySelect)

# build a test data frame
  test.data.df<-data.frame(x=1:138,y=filtered.data[idx+1])
 
# NB: must build a JSON string for dynamic title of vAxis
# see: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14080344/gvisscatterchart-define-series-dynamically

# Build JSON string, casting a character -- codeToName[idx] -- as a...character?!
myVAxis <- toJSON(list(title=as.character(codeToName[idx])))  # this works...

cat(myVAxis,'\n')
# example output of call to cat()
# {
# "title": "pH (NBS)"
# } 

  gvisScatterChart(test.data.df,
                   options=list(title=paste(codeToNameRw[idxRw],codeToName[idx],'(2012)'),
                               vAxis=myVAxis,
                                hAxis="{title:'2012'}",
                                width=500,height=400)
                                )
})
